newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Yang the most popular top-job candidate - polls.
newsitem.headline: HK's Yang the most popular top-job candidate - polls.

text.p: Hong Kong's former chief justice Sir Ti Liang Yang is the most popular declared candidate for chief executive of the territory after Britain hands it back to China next year, according to newspaper polls on Sunday.
Yang scored a popularity rating of 29.7 percent in a survey commissioned by the English-language South China Morning Post, which conducted the poll on Thursday and Friday.
Shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa, who confirmed his candidacy on Friday, secured a rating of 23.3 percent. Business tycoon Peter Woo, another declared candidate, received 8.5 percent backing.
Anson Chan, Governor Chris Patten's deputy who has consistently been the top choice of Hong Kong people as the next leader, had the poll's highest rating of 31.5 percent.
But she has not expressed an interest in the job.

In a separate survey conducted by Ming Pao Daily News, Yang won the support of 33 percent of the respondents, followed by Tung's 25 percent, Woo's eight percent and Li's five percent. The remaining 29 percent of respondents had no opinion.
The Post polled 624 people, and Ming Pao 759.
Hong Kong reverts to China next July 1 to become a Special Administrative Region under a leader to be chosen next month by a Beijing-controlled 400-member Selection Committee now being formed.
